text:
Mika Zibanejad has a five-game point streak and recently climbed into rarefied Rangers company, the kind of milestone that only comes after 751 games in New York. His two goals in Calgary, in the Rangers' last game at the Saddledome, were the first sign of the finishing coming back. He has 19 points in 21 games, mostly as a setup man (14 assists).

The goal total is the interesting part. Five goals on 5.05 expected is exactly fair, but his own shot quality is down: 0.71 expected goals per 60, against 1.02 last season. He's creating more for others than for himself. With him on the ice at five on five the Rangers take 52% of the chances, a shade below their team rate, and the shot-attempt share (44%) is the weakest of the regulars, which is why our model sees chances against pile up with him on. Our numbers say the line is getting a little unlucky, 2.3 goals below expected with him out there.

At 33, he's still a big-minutes centre and a power-play threat, with Evolving-Hockey crediting most of his value last season to the man advantage. Watch whether the shot volume from the slot comes back.
